conviction_note: Consensus (10 contributors, published by TOMRA 2026-10-14) sits almost exactly on the company's own mechanical guides (Recycling 52.4 = 50% x 105 backlog, Food 78.9 = 65% x 121, Collection 203 inside the 400-440 H2 range), so the quarter itself is unlikely to surprise much and the move lives in order intake and any change to the divisional FY guides; the one unpriced-looking positive is PLS's P2000 FID on 2026-10-16, which firmed up TOMRA Mining's 22-sorter award after consensus was compiled, so p_up leans slightly up (54) on a 10% scale because this name moves a median 12.8% on results days in either direction. Findings sum +1.1; the scaled number +0.8 is smaller because most of the sum is an order of unknown value that may only show up as after-quarter commentary.

already_public.what: Q3 divisional guides from the Q2 report: Collection H2 revenue 400-440 MEUR with GM above 40% and quarterly opex ~52 MEUR; Recycling FY 200-215 MEUR with 50% backlog conversion next quarter at 45-50% GM; Food FY 340-360 MEUR with 65% conversion and 43-47% GM in H2
Company-published sell-side consensus for 3Q26: revenue 347.0, EBITA adj 41.0 (median 41.7, range 36-45), EPS adj 0.065; Recycling orders 56.0, Food orders 83.1
LOI to become preferred RVM supplier to a leading international UK retail chain, ~2,000 installations, deliveries from 2027
No profit warning (resultatvarsel) or other guidance correction on NewsWeb between the Q2 report and the print; TOMRA dropped pre-close calls in July 2025

new_in_release.expect: EBITA adj near 41 MEUR; little surprise expected because consensus is built from the company's own conversion ratios. Collection gross margin, now that Poland installations have peaked, is the line most able to move.
Q3 order intake in Recycling (consensus 56) and Food (83). Recycling up on mining (the PLS P2000 award, either booked in Q3 or flagged as received after the quarter). Food unknown.

New Q4 backlog conversion ratios, plus FY Recycling (200-215) and Food (340-360) guides either reiterated or narrowed. Recycling's FY guide needs Q4 revenue of about 60-75 MEUR. That is feasible on seasonality (Q4 2025 was 75), so a cut is possible but unevidenced. Direction unknown.
UK, Spain and Greece timing commentary. The 2027+ framework is likely held back for the 24 November Capital Markets Update.

findings.finding: PLS reached FID on its P2000 Pilgangoora expansion on 2026-10-16, after TOMRA's consensus was compiled (2026-10-14). That firms up the pre-FID award to TOMRA Mining of 22 XRT ore sorters ('the world's largest sensor-based sorting plant', first reported 2026-08-24/25). Recycling order intake or after-quarter order commentary should therefore exceed a consensus (56, max 59) that does not appear to include it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Recycling order and sentiment lines have driven the large moves. Q1 2026 fell 25.6% with Recycling profitability among the causes. Q2 2026 rose 11.9% on a print that included the first Recycling order growth in over a year (+40%, mining and metals).
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus Recycling order intake (avg 56, median 58, max 59) is flat on Q2's 58, so no contributor added a 22-sorter order on top. The FID is an ASX disclosure by a counterparty, not a TOMRA release, and the stock has not moved on it (92.3 NOK on 10-15/16/22, against 89.2-91.35 around it). If it were priced, the Recycling order estimates would sit well above Q2. The contract value is not public, which caps the size.
findings.independence: The award itself, from a different source and date: https://www.globalminingreview.com/mining/25082026/pls-awards-tomra-mining-contract-for-a-22-sorter-installation-at-pilgangoora-the-worlds-largest-sensor-based-sorting-plant/ (2026-08-25, pre-FID, subject to FID). TOMRA's Q2 report says Recycling orders were already 'driven by metals recycling and mining'.

findings.finding: TOMRA signed an LOI on 2026-10-21 to be preferred RVM supplier to a leading international UK retailer (~2,000 installations, sales, leasing and service, deliveries from 2027). This adds to July's ~1,200-machine UK appointment and gives the Q3 report a quantifiable UK pipeline to talk to, but rival Envipco has also won several UK chains since July.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The July 2026 UK appointment came the evening before the Q2 print (+11.9%). A large Poland order on 2025-10-16 moved the stock about +3.5% intraday, from -2% to +1.57%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the stock was flat (92.3) on 10-22, the session after the release. The only residual is that management can put a number on 2027 UK volumes on the call. Sized small for that reason.
findings.independence: Envipco on NewsWeb (2026-09-23, 09-28, 07-29, 07-14) shows the competitor also winning UK chains, which tempers the share read: https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/list?issuer=ENVIP&fromDate=2026-07-01&toDate=2026-10-23

findings.finding: France dropped its plans for a mandatory national deposit system on 2026-09-07, and TOMRA fell about 8% that day on 2.7m shares. Pareto valued France at NOK 6-7 per share, and consensus had no French contribution before 2029-30. Management will be asked about it, but the damage is in the price.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-09-07: -8.3% close to close on the news itself (97.1 from 105.9).

findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: the stock fell 8% on the day and has not recovered (92.3 against 105.9 before). The only residual is a management comment that confirms or softens it.

baseline_tension: Mild agreement. The 5-day run-up (+3.4%) and the near-zero lean say little, and the slight positive lean comes from one counterparty FID, not from the tape. The 60-day -12% de-rating, after the France and Q1 drops, means expectations are not stretched.
language_note: Norwegian-language sources added nothing the English ones did not. TOMRA files on NewsWeb in English, and e24's Norwegian coverage after Q2 is one paywalled France article (2026-09-08) and no Q3 preview.

Swedish-language Finwire copy on placera.se, a Nordic-language source though not Norwegian, carried the two items the English search did not surface directly: why the stock fell on 2026-09-07 (France dropped its mandatory national DRS, Pareto valuing France at NOK 6-7 per share with consensus carrying nothing before 2029-30) and SB1 Markets' pre-Q3 note (EBITA ~43 MEUR in line, TP 115).
lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide': TOMRA re-guides every division every quarter (conversion ratios, FY revenue ranges), and the numbers are not pre-released. abs_move_pct goes from 9.0 to 10.0. The name's own results-day median of 12.8% is context, not a cap.
'A zero on a register that read is the truncation floor': positioning_check rewritten to say there is no anchor and the lean is the run-up. No size changed.
Finding sizes and p_up unchanged. No pre-release, offer period or one-off was in play, so no other rule bit.
